title: Company Access, Change, and Supplier Playbook (2025)
body:
> **Archived 2025-09-12:** this page is superseded by "Company Access, Change, and Supplier Playbook" and is kept for reference only.

Overview

This playbook brings together Redwood's company-wide rules for access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel, and the standard internal templates. Requesters, approvers and operational teams should treat it as their main operational reference.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors and contingent workers.
- Covers corporate systems (G Suite, Okta, Redwood Console), infrastructure systems (redwood-iam, cluster-admin, provisioner), procurement and expense approvals, vendor onboarding/offboarding, and travel paid with company funds.
- Team-specific technical runbooks still apply; this playbook defines the approval flows, classification and control gates around them.

Roles and Responsibilities

- Requester: raises access/change/procurement/travel requests with justification and cost estimate.
- Approver: the person(s) named in the approval matrix who confirm business need, least-privilege fit and budget.
- Security Owner: assesses data classification impact and authorizes access to sensitive resources.
- Procurement Owner (Finance): checks vendor contracts, tax paperwork and budget.
- IT/Platform: carries out approved changes, provisions access and keeps logs.
- Vendor Manager: owns the vendor relationship, renewals, SLAs and offboarding.

Approval Matrix (summary)

| Item Category | Typical Approver | Additional Approvals Required | Approval SLA |
|---------------|------------------|------------------------------|--------------|
| Standard SaaS user access | Team Lead | None | 48 hours |
| Admin access to production | Engineering Manager + Security Owner | CTO for >30 days | 24 hours |
| Infrastructure change (non-prod) | Service Owner | SRE review for risk > medium | 48 hours |
| Infrastructure change (prod) | SRE Lead + Change Manager | Security + Product if user-facing | 4 hours planned window |
| Procurement < $5k | Requester's Manager | Finance automated approval | 72 hours |
| Procurement $5k-$50k | Manager + Procurement Owner | Legal review if contract | 10 business days |
| Procurement > $50k | Exec Sponsor + Procurement Owner + Legal | Procurement Committee | 20 business days |

Access and Permissions

Principles
- Least privilege is the default.
- Elevated access is time-bounded (7-90 days by default, depending on role).
- Privileged access requires MFA and recorded sessions (redwood-iam + session-replay).

Standard Procedures
1. Submit a request in the Access Portal (https://internal.redwood/access) with business justification, role, resources and duration.
2. The portal suggests least-privilege roles from profile templates.
3. The manager approves; sensitive access also goes to the Security Owner.
4. IT/Platform provisions with an expiry date and sends the onboarding checklist.
5. Managers receive quarterly entitlement review emails; findings must be remediated within 14 days.

Example CLI (temporary privileged access):

redwood-iam grant-temporary --user alice@redwood.com --role infra-admin --duration 72h --justification "hotfix for KV cache"

Change Management

Policy Summary
- Every production-impacting change goes on the Change Calendar and through Change Approval. Emergency changes are reviewed after the fact.
- Categories: Standard, Normal, Emergency.

Change Process (Normal)
1. Open a change request in Change Tracker with the CI/CD link, rollback plan and blast radius estimate.
2. Run pre-deployment checks: integration tests, canary config, perf smoke test.
3. Collect approvals: Service Owner -> SRE -> Change Manager -> Security (if sensitive).
4. Book the Change Calendar slot and notify on-call.
5. Execute in the approved window, recording runbook steps.
6. Validate: health checks, telemetry review, error budget impact.
7. Close out with a short summary in the tracker within 24 hours.

Emergency Change Process
- During an incident an engineer may apply an Emergency Change with approval from the on-call SRE and a ping in Slack #oncall-exec. Log the change and open a postmortem within 72 hours.

Change Categorization Table

| Category | Definition | Expected Approval Path |
|----------|------------|------------------------|
| Standard | Repeatable, low-risk, pre-approved checklist | Auto-approved by Change Manager |
| Normal | New change needing explicit approvals | Service Owner -> SRE -> Change Manager |
| Emergency | Immediate mitigation of an active incident | On-call SRE -> Exec ping; retrospective required |

Data Management and Classification

Classification Levels
- Public: cleared for unrestricted release.
- Internal: non-sensitive internal information.
- Confidential: PII, business metrics, contractual information under access control.
- Restricted: regulated data (GDPR special categories, PCI) needing encryption at rest and in transit plus a data-handling SOP.

Data Handling Controls
- Confidential/Restricted data lives only in approved buckets with keys managed through customer-kms / redwood-kms.
- Confidential data must not go to personal email; Restricted sharing needs DLP approval.
- Retention follows the Data Retention Matrix (see templates).

Data Access Request Flow
1. File a Data Access Request (DAR) with dataset ID, reason and duration.
2. The Data Steward confirms need and assigns a reviewer.
3. The Security Owner checks the environment and approves if controls are adequate.
4. IT provisions scoped access, in a sandbox where possible.

Procurement and Expenses

Principles
- Vendor evaluation and negotiation are centralized for anything material (> $50k).
- Competitive procurement (at least two bids) is required for recurring spend > $10k/year.
- Company cards are for approved travel and low-value purchases only; exceptions need an approval ticket.

Procurement Workflow
1. Raise a Purchase Request in ProcureFlow with justification, budget code and contract term.
2. The Procurement Owner runs the vendor risk assessment (security questionnaire, SOC reports, references).
3. Legal reviews indemnity, data residency and termination clauses.
4. Finance allocates budget and issues the PO.
5. Proceed to vendor onboarding.

Expense Reimbursement
- Submit expenses via ExpenseBot within 60 days of purchase, with receipts.
- Non-compliant claims are returned for correction; repeat offenders are referred to people-ops.
- Per diem and travel allowance charts are in the Templates section.

Vendor Lifecycle and Management

Onboarding Checklist
- Complete the intake form in the Vendor Portal.
- Collect W-9 / W-8, SOC2 or other audit evidence, the security questionnaire and insurance certificates.
- Confirm data handling needs and put a DPA in place if the vendor processes personal data.
- Create the ERP vendor record and assign a Vendor Manager.

SLA and Risk Monitoring
- Vendors with production access or access to Confidential/Restricted data need an SLA and annually reviewed security attestations.
- Vendors are scored for confidentiality, criticality and financial stability and audited according to risk tier.

Offboarding
- Revoke accounts everywhere, retrieve or delete data per contract, and confirm return of company assets.
- Send the formal termination notice and file the contract in Contract Vault.

Travel Policy (summary)

Booking and Approvals
- Book all business travel through the Travel Portal (Concur) with manager pre-approval. Out-of-policy bookings may not be reimbursed.
- Use preferred airline and hotel vendors when available.

Spending Guidelines
- Economy class for flights < 6 hours. Business class permitted with Exec Sponsor approval for flights > 6 hours.
- Use the corporate negotiated hotel rate where possible.

Travel Safety and Data
- Devices taken on travel must have disk encryption and working VPN.
- Never keep Restricted data on personal devices.

Internal Templates and Forms

- Access request template: /templates/access-request.md
- Change request template: /templates/change-request.yml
- Vendor intake form: /templates/vendor-intake.xlsx
- Data Retention Matrix: /templates/data-retention.csv
- Expense report template: /templates/expense-template.xlsx

Template Example: change-request.yml
---
title: "Change Request"
service: "<service-name>"
author: "<your-name>"
change_type: "normal | standard | emergency"
rollback_plan: "|\n  - step1\n  - step2"
impact_area: "<prod|non-prod>"
scheduled_window: "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ"
prechecks: "smoke-tests, canary"
post_validation: "metrics: latency, error-rate"
---

Audit, Monitoring and Reporting

- Approvals and provisioning events are written to the immutable Audit Ledger. Procurement and vendor contracts are retained 7 years; 1 year for access logs unless tied to security investigations.
- A monthly compliance report covers access requests past SLA, open vendor risks and change window violations.

Enforcement and Exceptions

- Exceptions need a documented risk acceptance ticket approved by the business owner and the Security Owner, reviewed quarterly.
- Noncompliance leads to a remediation plan; repeated violations go to people-ops and may affect compensation.

Continuous Improvement

- Finance, Security and People-Ops review this playbook twice a year. Submit suggestions through the Policy Update form; significant changes are announced with a 14-day comment period.

Appendices

A. Quick Contact List
- Change Manager: change-manager@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Vendor Manager: vendor-manager@redwood.com
- Security Owner: security-policy@redwood.com

B. Common Scenarios
- "How do I get read-only access to analytics?" - File an Access Request -> Team Lead approves -> read-only access for 90 days.
- "Urgent security patch outside the maintenance window" - Run an Emergency Change with on-call SRE approval and log it.
